turns.user: Compare the free tiers of Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare Pages for a small side project.
turns.answer:
All three work for a small side project. Cloudflare Pages is the most generous for static sites. Vercel's free tier is non-commercial only, and Netlify's is now a small credit pool. Figures are from vendor pages dated 5–82 days ago, as of 11 Nov 2026.

| | Vercel Hobby | Netlify Free | Cloudflare Pages Free |
|---|---|---|---|
| Usage allowance | 100 GB fast data transfer, 1M function invocations | 300 credits/month, hard limit | Unlimited requests on a purely static project |
| Builds | 100 deployments/day | 15 credits per production deploy; 1 concurrent build | 500 builds/month, 1 at a time |
| Commercial use | Not allowed | Not shown in results | Not shown in results |
| At the limit | Capped, no extra purchases | Projects pause until next cycle | Not shown in results |

- **Netlify:** Accounts created after 4 Sept 2025 are on credit-based plans. Older accounts keep legacy plans, which had 100 GB bandwidth.
- **Cloudflare:** Single files are capped at 25 MiB. Adding Functions brings a daily request limit on the free Workers plan. Cloudflare also says new projects should start on Workers.

setup.user: Which managed Postgres hosting is cheapest for a small app: Neon, Supabase, or AWS RDS?
setup.answer:
Neon is usually the cheapest for a small app. Its free plan costs nothing, and its paid plan has no monthly minimum.

| As of 3 Nov 2026 | Free | Cheapest paid |
|---|---|---|
| Neon | $0, with 1 GB of storage per project and 100 CU-hours of compute | Typical spend is about $15/month for a small database on Launch; no minimum |
| Supabase | $0, with a 500 MB database; free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity | Pro is $25 plus compute, and one Small project comes to $30 after the $10 credit |
| AWS RDS | New accounts get up to $200 in credits, and the Free plan lasts up to 6 months | Pay per instance-hour plus storage, so it depends on the instance. I didn't pull a specific price. |

Neon also bills compute only while it's running. It scales to zero after 5 minutes idle. Supabase Pro compute is always on.

RDS is a good fit if you're already on AWS. For a small app, the free-tier credits run out, and I'd expect it to cost more than Neon's idle-friendly pricing. The cost comparison with Supabase's Pro plan comes from Neon's own guide, so treat it as vendor-sourced.

turns.user: Last Tuesday I asked you about Postgres hosting. Has any pricing changed since then?
turns.answer:
No price changes since our 3 Nov chat for any of the three. Every figure I gave then still matches the vendors' own pages. The one exception is Supabase's free-tier pause rule, which I couldn't confirm on a current page.

| Item | Then (3 Nov) | Now (11 Nov 2026) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Neon Free plan, Launch spend, minimum | $0, 1 GB, 100 CU-hours; about $15/mo; no minimum | $0 with no credit card: 100 projects, each with 100 CU-hours and 1 GB of storage; no monthly minimum… about $15/month for a small database on Launch | Held |
| Neon scale-to-zero | 5 min | after 5 minutes idle on the Free plan and Launch plan | Held |
| Supabase Free database | 500 MB | 500 MB per project | Held |
| Supabase Pro base, credit | $25; $10 credit | Paid plans include $10 in Compute Credits; Pro still $25 | Held |
| Supabase compute always on | Yes | charged for the exact number of hours that a project is running | Held |
| Supabase free pause | 1 week | Only on the pricing page, which is 403 days old | Couldn't verify |
| AWS RDS credits, free plan | Up to $200; 6 months | totaling $200; up to 6 months | Held |

One small catch: a Neon FAQ lists 0.5 GB of storage per project on Free. That's older wording. The pricing page and plan docs both say 1 GB. "Last Tuesday" here means 3 Nov, since we didn't talk on 10 Nov.

turns.answer:
Claude Pro costs $20 a month in the US, or $17 a month if you pay annually.

- Anthropic's pricing page lists $17 per month on an annual subscription ($200 billed up front), or $20 if billed monthly. That page copy is flagged as old, so I also checked a third-party tracker. It says those figures matched Anthropic's pricing page as of 10 November 2026.
- Anthropic's help page says pricing is in local currency where supported, and varies by region and tax treatment. Your price may differ from the US one. Check claude.ai/upgrade to see what you'd pay.

turns.answer:
The newest Opus is Claude Opus 5.5, and its API price is $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens. Anthropic's Opus page gives those figures and says they are 20% below Opus 5. That page is about 6 days old.

- **Cache reads:** $0.20 per million tokens.
- **Fast mode:** $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.
- **US-only inference:** 1.1x pricing for input and output tokens.
- **Opus 5 (the previous version):** $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens.

turns.user: Is GPT-4 still the newest OpenAI model?
turns.answer:
No, GPT-4 is several generations behind. OpenAI's newest model is GPT-6 Cyber. OpenAI introduced it on 5 November 2026 as a cybersecurity model for finding vulnerabilities and developing fixes. It's restricted, though. Organizations need approval through OpenAI's Daybreak program before they can call it.

The newest model most people can use is GPT-6.1 Terra. It's available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. It launched on 26 October 2026. Developers can also reach it through the API.

For the flagship, OpenAI describes GPT-6 Astra as its most intelligent and aligned model. Since 7 October, ChatGPT answers with GPT-6. That claim comes from a third-party roundup, not from OpenAI.
